$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the money-path file list (#1030).
This list previously existed in three places that disagreed. .github/labeler.yml
-- which applies the `money-path` label, and therefore decides whether money.md
and its characterization-test bar get loaded -- was MISSING the delegation rail,
the rail seam, and the SDK signer. Nobody noticed, because nothing compared them.
A money-path list that is wrong in one copy is worse than none: it reads as
coverage.
TWO LISTS, because the two consumers ask different questions:
globs -- RUNTIME money-path code. Code that moves money or grants authority,
i.e. behaviour the deployed money-flow QA harness actually exercises. This is
what scripts/ci/qa-freshness.mjs checks: 'did the green QA run cover this?'
controlGlobs -- the money-path SAFEGUARD's own control surface. A PR that
weakens the gate deserves the money-path playbook and a human reading it, but
re-running the money-flow harness proves nothing about a CI config change --
the harness does not test the gate. So these are LABELLED money-path without
forcing a QA re-run, which would be friction with no evidence attached.
labeler.yml uses the UNION. qa-freshness.mjs uses `globs` only.
scripts/ci/money-path.test.mjs asserts this file, labeler.yml and the SKILL.md
Merge Gate agree. Editing one without the others fails CI.
Adding a glob is cheap and safe. Leaving one out is the failure mode.
2026-07-27 (#1045): added the money-moving surfaces the adversarial review
found missing (sweep, relayer, safe-exec, approvals, hybrid-accounts,
mainnet-gate) -- 'leaving one out is the failure mode', and these were out.
release-bump.mjs and publish.yml moved to controlGlobs: the harness cannot
exercise them, so keeping them in `globs` made 'a green run covered this'
hollow -- they still get the label and the human reading, without a QA
re-run that proves nothing about them.
2026-08-19 (#1607): infra/relayer.ts widened to infra/relayer*.ts (spend guard,
balance monitor) and infra/outbound-*.ts added -- epic #1554 shipped the durable
outbound queue + bump worker, which broadcast and replace real transactions.
2026-08-23 (#1892): routes/agent-rekey.ts and modules/agents/rekey-*.ts added.
#1698 shipped the re-key surface -- it revokes and re-issues an agent's on-chain
spend authority, the identical job routes/agent-delegations.ts was already listed
for -- and NOTHING learned about it: not this file, not labeler.yml, not the
SKILL.md Merge Gate. PR #1891 changed routes/agent-rekey.ts and carried
`area:backend, area:docs` and NO money-path label; the classification was right
only because a human had labelled the ISSUE. Note infra/repositories/** already
covered the re-key REPOSITORY, so a PR touching the storage layer was labelled
while one touching only the route was not -- the most misleading kind of
half-coverage, because the list read as though it knew about re-key.
2026-08-23 (#1892, from review): infra/delegate-*.ts added. The delegate
balance monitor (#714, epic #713) is the DETECT mitigation for the x402
in-flight window -- the interval where Safe-funded USDC sits on a hot
delegate EOA outside every policy layer -- and it alerts on `lingering`,
i.e. sweepable money nobody swept. Its sibling infra/relayer-balance-monitor.ts
is EQUALLY read-only and was already matched by infra/relayer*.ts; the two
even share the DELEGATE_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL channel. Listing one and not the
other was an accident of glob prefix, not a judgement. Globbed rather than
named so the next delegate-* infra file is covered the day it is written,
same reasoning as #1607's relayer.ts -> relayer*.ts widening.
2026-08-23 (#1897): modules/machine-payments/** REMOVED -- retired
deliberately, not lost. It matched nothing, and it never had: the directory
does not appear anywhere in git history, under any status. #1158 added it
PRE-EMPTIVELY for the #997 split ('machine-payments (pre-emptive)', commit
808394bf), and that split landed as modules/mpp/ instead, so the anticipated
destination was never created. This is therefore a deletion, not a re-point:
there is no moved code to follow. Every machine-payment file that exists
today was already covered by a DIFFERENT entry -- routes/machine-payments.ts
and domain/machine-payment-lifecycle.ts by name, infra/repositories/
machine-payments.ts by infra/repositories/**, the five machine_payment_*
migrations by db/migrations/**, and the module itself by modules/mpp/**.
Proven, not asserted: classifying every tracked file through
qa-freshness.mjs's own matchesGlob() before and after the removal returns
the IDENTICAL set. The perimeter did not shrink.
A phantom entry is not free, which is why it came out: this list is read by
humans and agents deciding whether their own diff is money-path, and an entry
naming a module layout that never existed makes the perimeter look like it
covers ground it does not. money-path.test.mjs now asserts every glob matches
at least one tracked file, so a fifth phantom cannot accumulate silently.
Adding a glob AHEAD of the code it anticipates is still allowed -- see
PRE_EMPTIVE_GLOBS in that test, which is the sanctioned place to say so.
